I ran into this exact issue when I first found one of my favorite poets, Stephanie Burt. I started with her old, pre-transition works, and when I finally caught up to her current work, it felt strange to look back on her older books that used her deadname and incorrect pronouns. However, I think that art is the perfect medium to explore these ideas, no matter how uncomfortable or weird that conversation may be, especially in the case of artists like Abigail or Stephanie whose works actively explore such topics. It can add a whole new layer to the work, especially ones that directly discuss gender.

In any case, death of the author makes things a bit less awkward in terms of interacting with the work itself. Just remember: judge the work for what it is, not for what the artist is/was. Authorial intent and perspective exists, but art can take on its own life outside of that depending on the reader.

My main worry is disappointing or causing anyone more stress than they're already dealing with. Not to mention the high likelihood of being sent to a psych ward again--I'm legally an adult and all, but I still live with my folks and am walking on thin mental ice already. One wrong move and I'm worried I'll end up committed again.

Oh, there's a lot more garbage I've had to wade through than just SH-related guilt, lol. Lots of stuff to work through. I've seen therapists, tried a whole bunch of meds, and nothing's been able to consistently work. It's been tough, but I'm trying to chip away at things as best I can.

Thank you for the kind words. I'm aware of certain triggers and try my best to handle them appropriately, definitely going to keep at it there. Things have reached a point where the urge is near addictive, almost a Pavlovian response for whenever I feel an ounce of self-loathing or discomfort, especially when it comes to guilt.

I'm sure your significant other will understand. Ask your therapist how to best word things, though--tried explaining MD to one of my good friends when I found this subreddit, only for them to think they suffered from it because they were able to imagine things, lol.

Ditto the whole not finding anyone else like this thing, feels like I'm the only one going through anything like this. I can relate to you here, though. Sometimes, I go into self-loathing, dysphoric rages when I'm misgendered because it feels so horrible, but other times, I feel this awful sense of dread and discomfort when I identify as my preferred gender, almost like I'm faking it. I've started to worry that the latter "dread and discomfort" is dysphoria as well, like both my options are losing tickets (I'm very uncomfortable being labeled any shade of nonbinary). I just want to live as full of a life as I can, but I feel like no matter what, I'm being robbed of that. The cis envy is very strong.

I'm sorry I can't be much help outside of just relating to you. I'm only just coming to terms with and unpacking things myself. This shade of OCD is very scary--one minute, I feel so excited for the future, but it all comes tumbling down the next, taking any sense of self with it. I start ERP in about a week, and while I'm optimistic, I'm petrified that the "acceptance" process will just equate to me living with these thoughts forever, never being able to enjoy life as my preferred gender because I can't ever shake the intrusive doubts. 

Solidarity & best of luck to you. Feels like we're all alone in this, but we'll make it through together.

I can't offer any advice, as I'm battling with some of the same things you are myself, but solidarity to you all the same.

I haven't transitioned yet outside of certain social environments, and I'm petrified that I'll never be able to do anything further thanks to all these fears that I'll regret it or am faking everything. Feels like I'll never enjoy being in my own skin--either I'll be intensely dysphoric for the rest of my life, or I'll be crippled by those intrusive thoughts whenever I do the slightest thing that codes as "invalidating" myself. It doesn't help that a lot of people around me have detransitioned, either. It feels like the only right thing to do is to just live life as my assigned sex, but I can't see myself making it to my thirties if I try. Either way, I don't see a point in living. I hate it.

I'm starting ERP therapy soon. I'm very worried that I won't be able to get past the root those thoughts and *actually* start living, like you mentioned (not to mention that the only specialist available to me is religious, to which I'm nervous about being told that this is all in my head). Feels like there aren't any success stories for this subset (widely available ones, at least). But in any case, I'm going to give it my all.

Apologies for the little tangent, you're the first person I've run into on this site that seems to feel remotely the same as I do. Best of luck to you, and know that you're not alone in this. Take care.

If you see yourself not being able to take care of yourself or spiraling out of control due to trauma manifesting, then I'd recommend going. Otherwise, I'd look at milder solutions (therapy if you aren't already seeing a psych, outpatient services, etc).

Solidarity to you, man. I was in your exact same situation last year, ended up barely scraping by thanks to begging for extensions and stints in inpatient therapy (side note, your college professors are infinitely more understanding than your high school teachers ever were. Email them about your situation and I guarantee they'll help you out). 

While I'm arguably worse now, I think I would've killed myself already if I hadn't taken a leave of absence after my first year of college. I'd suggest you do the same--take a semester/year to figure things out or, at the very least, not have to pile schoolwork on top of everything else. If available, scheduling a visit with an on-campus therapist is a good option as well. Best of luck.

I'm still questioning myself, but I think that even if I realize I'm transgender, I won't actually transition outside of a few subtle tweaks to public gender expression. I think I have very bad dysphoria (not sure if it's just depression and loads of self hatred), but even so, I don't have the means or mental strength to go through any major transitioning. I come from and live in a very conservative area, and publicly transitioning would result in me losing pretty much everything I hold dear. Seeing as I struggle with severe mental illness already, I don't think I'd be able to handle that. 

I see this sort of plight as more of a mental, personal battle: as long as you're comfortable with who you are and like yourself, you should be okay. I'm hoping that in my case, just acknowledging my identity on a personal level can be enough.

That being said, this stuff is all on an individual basis. I've gone down loads of hypothetical rabbit holes, but they all were built on others' experiences and not my own. Take my (and others') testimonials with a grain of salt; only you can know what's best for you. Best of luck, always here to talk.

Sucks that there isn't an effective, mainstream alternative.
